1.explanation: When the KML parser reads the <name> element it uses getAllTextContent (from ol/xml.js) to collect the raw node text. If the name was wrapped in CDATA or contains an XML entity (e.g. '), getAllTextContent simply concatenates the text nodes without resolving those entity codes. The un-decoded string then flows into KML.readNameFromNode and ultimately into createNameStyleFunction (and the style function created by createFeatureStyleFunction), which assign the literal "'" to the Text style. To fix the bug you either need to extend getAllTextContent/_ to replace known XML entities (e.g. ' → ') or decode the string in readNameFromNode or in createNameStyleFunction before handing it off to the renderer.
1.bug_scenario: When reading KML placemarks that contain XML character entity references (for example <name>Andy&apos;s Pub</name>), the map labels render the raw entity “'” instead of an apostrophe. In the screenshot you can see the label “Andy&apos;s Pub, Terrasse” drawn on the map, whereas the decoded text “Andy’s Pub, Terrasse” appears correctly elsewhere (e.g. in the feature list).

2.explanation: The KML class in KML.js is responsible for parsing the <name> element and turning it into a label. The methods readName and readNameFromNode extract text via getAllTextContent but never decode HTML/XML entities, so the literal sequence “'” remains in the string. Then createNameStyleFunction takes that un-decoded string and sets it as the Text style value, leading to labels showing “'” instead of an apostrophe. To fix the bug, entity decoding (or a call to decodeURIComponent on the extracted name) needs to be inserted in these methods before the text is handed off to the Text style.
2.bug_scenario: The screenshots show a KML‐based map with placemark labels. Although the underlying KML data contains a name of "Andy&apos;s" (i.e. the apostrophe is encoded as an XML entity), the rendered label on the map literally displays “Andy&apos;s Pub, Terrasse” instead of decoding the entity to “Andy's Pub, Terrasse.”
